title: echelon.routes/v1 — a Limen application's route inventory
description: The URL space of an application, as .echelon/routes.json (LCP-107, LCP-108). Rendered by the Limen routing libraries (TypeScript renderRouteInventory, F# Inventory.render), byte-identical between them: keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit, two-space indentation, a final newline. Praxis (praxis foundations verify) and Conditor validate it without running the application. Changes within v1 are additive only. Validators accept unknown properties, so a document from a later v1 library still validates under an earlier v1 schema.

mode.description: Where the routed location lives: the fragment (#/path?query, the default for static hosts) or the document path and query.

home.description: The home route: where a refused return target and the way home lead.

signIn.description: The sign-in route, which carries the return target as its returnTo query parameter.

notFound.description: The route whose match is the NotFound outcome, usually a top-level {*rest}.

routes.description: Every destination that is not a redirect, in table order.

legacy.description: Every redirect: legacy entries (legacy-1, legacy-2, …) and redirect routes of the table. Never produced when building a location.

routeName.description: A destination's full name: its chain's names joined by '.'.

pattern.description: '/' followed by the chain's segments: literals, {name:type} parameters and a final {*name} wildcard.

default.description: The value reported when the key is absent and omitted from the canonical form, as JSON (a date YYYY-MM-DD and a month YYYY-MM as text, a set as a sorted array), or null.

values.description: The values of an enum or set; null otherwise, and for a set that allows any non-empty member.

params.description: Path parameters, then query parameters, parent first, in declaration order.

guards.description: The guard names along the chain, outermost first. A guard decides the interface, never access.

requires.description: Resource keys the engine loads before rendering, the union along the chain.

returnTarget.description: Whether a sign-in may return here (never the sign-in or not-found route).

params.description: The target's parameters: '{source}' copies a parameter of the pattern; anything else is literal.
